title: Make Windows broker control polling nonblocking
description:
PREREQUISITE for task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 (Durable Claude attempt dispatch).

Fresh real-Windows measurement on Windows 10.0.26200 / Node 24.16 with the actual release broker and copied harmless executables found the public Claude launcher cannot complete a normal provider run lasting more than the broker's first 50ms wait slice. `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/src/watch.rs:23-43` documents the production defect: after the first slice it calls synchronous `read_frame` on silent-open fd0, blocks, and cannot observe the later child exit. The parent then reaches its timeout, closes/destroys provider streams, and the public launcher returns exact `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_STREAM_ERROR@OUTPUT` instead of PROVEN. Direct boundary measurement likewise resolves only at the parent timeout. No COMPLETED frame exists before timeout, so changing TypeScript `BrokerSession.onCompleted` cannot fix this pre-terminal deadlock.

Deliverable: make post-LAUNCH control observation nonblocking without weakening CANCEL, EOF, framing, containment, or stream-evidence rules. Keep Win32 unsafe calls inside `boundary.rs`; expose an explicit readiness/pending decision through the broker byte-channel contract and have `watch.rs` wait in bounded slices while consuming control only when ready. Do not infer pending from EOF, copy OS authority outside the boundary, ignore cancellation, add a launcher dependency-injection seam, or use a mock-backed positive proof.

Expected owned scope for architect remeasurement: `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/src/frames.rs`, `boundary.rs`, `watch.rs`, `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/Cargo.toml` if the pinned windows-sys Pipes feature is required, and one focused existing/new broker test path. NOT in scope: daemon dispatch, grant authority, runtime hydration, review, or E2E canary.
definitionOfDone: A real Windows conformance test using the actual built broker and a harmless provider that remains alive beyond 50ms then exits naturally completes before the configured timeout and the public launcher returns OBSERVED/PROVEN with nonempty, complete stdout/stderr evidence.

Post-LAUNCH silent-open control is represented as PENDING, never EOF or a protocol refusal; actual EOF, a legal CANCEL, malformed/duplicate frames, and readiness API failure each retain their exact stable reason/layer and containment behavior.
Cancellation remains prompt and bounded, provider descendants remain Job-contained, and no path ignores fd0 until the 30-minute broker timeout.

Win32 calls/unsafe code remain confined to the production boundary module; no deep import, mock boundary, test-only production branch, whole-launch seam, or locally restated launcher authority is introduced.
TDD and a mutation drill prove the readiness gate is load-bearing; runner Rust/TypeScript tests and real Windows conformance execute with nonzero test counts.
taskRails: Use TDD; every refusal asserts its exact stable reason code and layer, and any generated sweep asserts exact nonzero cardinality.
Keep each production source <=250 physical lines and the plan <=10 affected files.
The positive proof must use the real Windows broker/launcher boundary; a scripted ByteChannel test alone cannot certify the defect.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the minimum nonblocking byte/framing contract without a fail-open default. Add required `ByteChannel::poll_read(&mut self, &mut [u8]) -> Result<core::task::Poll<usize>, u32>`: Pending means silent/open, Ready(0) means real EOF, Ready(n>0) means exactly n bytes were consumed. Keep blocking `read` only for the initial LAUNCH and other already-bounded phases. Add private child module frames/polling.rs with a stateful frame accumulator retained across wait slices; it incrementally fills the fixed six-byte header and then the already-bounded payload, returns Pending without losing partial bytes, maps Ready(0) at any incomplete stage to the existing FrameTruncated path, maps syscall errors through ProtocolError::channel, rejects a channel reporting more bytes than offered, and never allocates from the declared length until the shared version/cap validator has accepted it. Factor that header validation once in frames.rs so blocking and polled decoding cannot disagree; preserve zero-length payloads and every existing reason/stage. Use `core::task::Poll` so no new root vocabulary/lib.rs edit is needed. Update all four non-production ByteChannel implementors explicitly—frame_sweep, session, idempotence, containment—rather than adding a default that could silently block a future production channel. Keep frames.rs and the new child each <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note: Nonblocking byte/framing contract landed with no fail-open default. ByteChannel gained REQUIRED `poll_read(&mut self, &mut [u8]) -> Result<core::task::Poll<usize>, u32>` (Pending = silent/open, Ready(0) = real EOF, Ready(n) = n consumed); blocking `read` kept for LAUNCH. Header judgement factored once into `frames::validate_header` -> Result<(u8, usize)>, used by both decoders, so version-before-cap order cannot drift. New private child `frames/polling.rs` holds `PolledFrames`: a per-channel accumulator that keeps partial header/payload across Pending turns, sizes its read request as (FRAME_HEADER_BYTES + kind.max_payload()) - held so a peer cannot grow it, maps Ready(0) at any incomplete stage to FrameTruncated, maps poll syscall errors through ProtocolError::channel, refuses a channel reporting more bytes than offered with channel(0), and never allocates from a declared length before validate_header accepts it. Zero-length payloads still decode. All four non-production implementors updated explicitly (session/frame_sweep/idempotence/containment) with semantics matching each harness: scripted PollStep table in session (panics by name if the script runs dry, falls back to `read` only when unscripted), read-equivalent in frame_sweep/containment (a drained tape is a closed peer, so existing empty-fd0 ControlEnded cases keep meaning), and bytes-before-ended-else-Pending in idempotence so the three-way race stays a race. implementationPlan.description: Wire the real single-threaded Windows boundary and watch loop. Add the exact pinned windows-sys `Win32_System_Pipes` feature only (Cargo.lock must not change). In boundary.rs—and nowhere else—call `PeekNamedPipe` with `lpTotalBytesAvail`: success/zero is Poll::Pending; success/nonzero performs `ReadFile` for at most min(total available, caller-buffer length), so it cannot wait for more bytes; ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE is Poll::Ready(0), preserving real EOF; every other GetLastError value is returned verbatim. No other reader exists in the broker, so bytes observed available cannot be stolen between peek and bounded read. In watch.rs, retain one accumulator for the entire post-LAUNCH loop, wait in the existing <=50ms slices, and poll control after each nonterminal slice: Pending continues, a complete frame goes through the existing AcceptState, EOF keeps ControlEnded, and a polling error uses the existing exact protocol refusal/unwind. Keep shutdown-first, timeout, CANCEL, abandoned-wait, natural completion, and exactly-once Job containment ordering unchanged. Replace the obsolete known-blocking comment with the new partial-frame/nonblocking invariant; add no new protocol code/version and no unsafe/Win32 call outside boundary.rs.
implementationPlan.note: Real Windows boundary and watch loop wired; the pre-terminal deadlock is gone at the Rust layer. Cargo.toml gained exactly one feature, "Win32_System_Pipes", on the same =0.61.2 pin; `git diff --exit-code -- native/Cargo.lock` is clean. boundary.rs `PipeChannel::poll_read` peeks with PeekNamedPipe reading ONLY lpTotalBytesAvail (buffer/bytes-read/bytes-left-this-message all null, since bytes-left is documented zero for a byte-mode pipe), then ReadFile for at most min(available, buffer.len()) so it can never wait for bytes the peer has not written: available==0 is Poll::Pending, ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE from either call is Poll::Ready(0) (real EOF, same fold `read` already used), every other GetLastError is returned verbatim. The single-reader premise is stated in the SAFETY prose as a condition that must change with any future second reader. All unsafe/Win32 stays in boundary.rs: `grep -rl "unsafe|windows_sys" broker/src` outside it hits only pre-existing prose in descriptors.rs/launch.rs/verify.rs and the pre-existing handle_probe bin, none of which my diff touches. watch.rs builds ONE PolledFrames before the loop and reuses it every turn, calls poll_frame only after a nonterminal <=50ms slice, and maps Pending->continue (no refusal), Ready(frame)->existing AcceptState, FrameTruncated->ControlEnded + ChannelEnded note, other errors->refuse_protocol/ControlRefused. Shutdown-first, abandoned wait, timeout, CANCEL and exactly-once containment ordering are untouched; the obsolete KNOWN LIMITATION block is replaced by the nonblocking/partial-frame invariant. No new protocol reason, stage or version. Fresh real Windows run, native toolchain, no WSL: `cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker` is green with 95 executed tests (89 baseline + 6 new), including all six named cases printed by name under --nocapture: silent_open_control_is_pending_while_a_longer_child_exits_naturally, fragmented_cancel_header_survives_pending_polls_and_stays_prompt, post_launch_eof_is_control_ended_not_a_protocol_refusal, partial_payload_then_pending_eof_is_control_ended_not_a_protocol_refusal, wrong_version_after_launch_refuses_at_protocol_framing, poll_failure_after_launch_refuses_with_exact_channel_failure_evidence. REVIEW FINDING, FIXED IN THIS STEP. `polling.rs:85` refuses a channel that reports more bytes than it was offered (`ProtocolError::channel(0)`), and NOTHING tested it: the scripted harness clamped every count with `count.min(buffer.len())`, so an over-report was not even representable. That is an unguarded production refusal branch under epic rail 6. Added `PollStep::Overreports` (returns `Ready(buffer.len() + 1)` having placed nothing — unreachable by writing bytes, hence a step and not a script) and the named case `a_poll_claiming_more_than_it_was_offered_refuses_as_a_broken_channel`, pinning ControlRefused, poll_calls 1, polled_bytes 0, `only_protocol_refusal == (RefusalLayer::Protocol.wire(), ProtocolReason::ChannelFailed.ordinal(), 0)`, stage Framing, terminate-job 1, accounting 1.
